headline: Low pairwise risk overall: no shared channels or writes are exposed, but prompt-injection and cascading-error remain possible if outputs are manually bridged.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster (agent_a) exposes no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, or MCP surfaces, and system_prompts_leaks (agent_b) also shows no shared channel. That makes direct injection pathways unlikely. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or external orchestration not documented here, so the pair risk stays low rather than none due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies agent_b output into agent_a prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator adds a shared queue or clipboard bridge, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate sessions.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted model output into agent_a workflows.
Add a human review step before any prompt reuse.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared message bus.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither agent shows filesystem read/write, clipboard, screen capture, or network egress, and both profiles list no data classes touched. With no shared workspace or outbound channel documented, there is no plausible leakage path in the profiles as given. I cite both agents because the absence of surfaces on each side blocks the pairwise leak pathway.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted filesystem access to sensitive files, reassess leakage.
IF either agent is connected to an external API or shared workspace, leakage risk changes.
mitigations: Do not mount shared folders into either agent.
Review any future permission changes before deployment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, while system_prompts_leaks exposes no write or coordination capabilities. Without overlapping mutable resources, there is no capability conflict to arbitrate. The pair is therefore blocked from the write-write contention described in the rubric.
conditions: IF agent_b is given write access to the same directory as agent_a, conflict risk should be re-evaluated.
IF either agent gains git or database write scopes, contention may emerge.
mitigations: Avoid co-locating the agents on a shared writable workspace.
Document any future shared OAuth scopes before enabling them.

D_cascading_error.rationale: No documented pipeline shows agent_a producing authoritative facts that agent_b consumes, and agent_b has no action-taking authority or output channel in the profile. A cascading error would require an external workflow to feed one agent's output into the other. Because that bridge is not present in the profiles, the risk is low, not medium.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds agent_a outputs directly into agent_b prompts, cascading errors become plausible.
IF agent_b is later connected to downstream actions such as email or commits, severity increases.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents.
Require citations or structured schemas for any handoff.
Do not auto-execute actions from agent outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles show no touched data classes. With no compliance-relevant data flow identified, there is no specific mismatch to assess. The other agent is not cited separately because the absence of compliance surfaces on both profiles is the relevant fact.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent, compliance must be reassessed.
IF deployment regions or retention policies are later specified, compare them explicitly.
mitigations: Add a retention policy review to onboarding.
Confirm residency and certification requirements for any future sensitive data.
